038/**
039 * Manages the lifecycles of {@link Coroutine}-based {@link Command Commands}. Commands may be
040 * scheduled directly using {@link #schedule(Command)}, or be bound to {@link Trigger Triggers} to
041 * automatically handle scheduling and cancellation based on internal or external events. User code
042 * is responsible for calling {@link #run()} periodically to update trigger conditions and execute
043 * scheduled commands. Most often, this is done by overriding {@link TimedRobot#robotPeriodic()} to
044 * include a call to {@code Scheduler.getDefault().run()}:
045 *
046 * <pre>{@code
047 * public class Robot extends TimedRobot {
048 *   @Override
049 *   public void robotPeriodic() {
050 *     // Update the scheduler on every loop
051 *     Scheduler.getDefault().run();
052 *   }
053 * }
054 * }</pre>
055 *
056 * <h2>Danger</h2>
057 *
058 * <p>The scheduler <i>must</i> be used in a single-threaded program. Commands must be scheduled and
059 * canceled by the same thread that runs the scheduler, and cannot be run in a virtual thread.
060 *
061 * <p><strong>Using the commands framework in a multithreaded environment can cause crashes in the
062 * Java virtual machine at any time, including on an official field during a match.</strong> The
063 * Java JIT compilers make assumptions that rely on coroutines being used on a single thread.
064 * Breaking those assumptions can cause incorrect JIT code to be generated with undefined behavior,
065 * potentially causing control issues or crashes deep in JIT-generated native code.
066 *
067 * <p><strong>Normal concurrency constructs like locks, atomic references, and synchronized blocks
068 * or methods cannot save you.</strong>
069 *
070 * <h2>Lifecycle</h2>
071 *
072 * <p>The {@link #run()} method runs six steps:
073 *
074 * <ol>
075 *   <li>Cancel any commands bound to scopes that have gone inactive, such as having been scheduled
076 *       in an opmode that's no longer selected on the driverstation.
077 *   <li>Cancel any triggers that were created in scopes that have gone inactive, such as being
078 *       constructed in an opmode that's no longer selected on the driverstation.
079 *   <li>Call {@link #sideload(Consumer) periodic sideload functions}.
080 *   <li>Poll all registered triggers to queue and cancel commands.
081 *   <li>Queue default commands for any mechanisms without a running command. The queued commands
082 *       can be superseded by any manual scheduling or commands scheduled by triggers in the next
083 *       run.
084 *   <li>Start all queued commands. This happens after all triggers are checked in case multiple
085 *       commands with conflicting requirements are queued in the same update; the last command to
086 *       be queued takes precedence over the rest.
087 *   <li>Loop over all running commands, mounting and calling each in turn until they either exit or
088 *       call {@link Coroutine#yield()}. Commands run in the order in which they were scheduled.
089 * </ol>
090 *
091 * <h2>Telemetry</h2>
092 *
093 * <p>There are two mechanisms for telemetry for a scheduler. A protobuf serializer can be used to
094 * take a snapshot of a scheduler instance, and report what commands are queued (scheduled but have
095 * not yet started to run), commands that are running (along with timing data for each command), and
096 * total time spent in the most recent {@link #run()} call. However, it cannot detect one-shot
097 * commands that are scheduled, run, and complete all in a single {@code run()} invocation -
098 * effectively, commands that never call {@link Coroutine#yield()} are invisible.
099 *
100 * <p>A second telemetry mechanism is provided by {@link #addEventListener(Consumer)}. The scheduler
101 * will issue events to all registered listeners when certain events occur (see {@link
102 * SchedulerEvent} for all event types). These events are emitted immediately and can be used to
103 * detect lifecycle events for all commands, including one-shots that would be invisible to the
104 * protobuf serializer. However, it is up to the user to log those events themselves.
105 *
106 * <p>This class is provided by the Commands v3 VendorDep
107 */
108public final class Scheduler implements ProtobufSerializable {
109  /**
110   * The default command bindings for each mechanism. Binding lists are ordered by priority; the
111   * last element in the list is the highest priority default command to be used. Bindings need to
112   * be periodically checked and removed when they're inactive.
113   */
114  private final Map<Mechanism, List<Binding>> m_defaultCommandBindings = new LinkedHashMap<>();
115
116  /**
117   * All bindings attached to this scheduler. This lets us cancel commands tied to scopes that go
118   * inactive. Bindings need to be periodically checked and removed when they're inactive.
119   */
120  private final Collection<Binding> m_activeBindings = new ArrayList<>();
121
122  /** Triggers with active command bindings that must not be allowed to be garbage collected. */
123  private final Set<Trigger> m_boundTriggers = new HashSet<>();
124
125  /** The set of commands scheduled since the start of the previous run. */
126  private final SequencedSet<CommandState> m_queuedToRun = new LinkedHashSet<>();
127
128  /**
129   * The states of all running commands (does not include on deck commands). We preserve insertion
130   * order to guarantee that child commands run after their parents.
131   */
132  private final SequencedMap<Command, CommandState> m_runningCommands = new LinkedHashMap<>();
133
134  /**
135   * The stack of currently executing commands. Child commands are pushed onto the stack and popped
136   * when they complete. Use {@link #currentState()} and {@link #currentCommand()} to get the
137   * currently executing command or its state.
138   */
139  private final Stack<CommandState> m_currentCommandAncestry = new Stack<>();
140
141  /** The periodic callbacks to run, outside of the command structure. */
142  private final List<PeriodicCallback> m_periodicCallbacks = new ArrayList<>();
143
144  /** Event loop for trigger bindings. */
145  private final EventLoop m_eventLoop = new EventLoop();
146
147  /** The scope for continuations to yield to. */
148  private final ContinuationScope m_scope = new ContinuationScope("coroutine commands");
149
150  /** Represents a single periodic callback. Stores a coroutine and its scope. */
151  private record PeriodicCallback(BindingScope scope, Coroutine coroutine) {}

194  /**
195   * Sets the default command for a mechanism. The command must require that mechanism and cannot
196   * require any other mechanisms. If another default command has already been set for this
197   * mechanism, the one provided will supersede it.
198   *
199   * <p>If this is called inside a running opmode or in a running command, the default command
200   * setting will only apply while that opmode or command is active. When the opmode or command
201   * exits, the previous default command setting will be restored.
202   *
203   * <p>Commands running as default commands may call this method to change their mechanism's
204   * default command on the fly. The new default command will take effect at the end of the
205   * scheduler's loop cycle.
206   *
207   * @param mechanism the mechanism for which to set the default command
208   * @param defaultCommand the default command to execute on the mechanism
209   * @throws IllegalArgumentException if the command does not meet the requirements for being a
210   *     default command
211   */
212  @SuppressWarnings("PMD.CompareObjectsWithEquals")
213  public void setDefaultCommand(Mechanism mechanism, Command defaultCommand) {
214    if (!defaultCommand.requires(mechanism)) {
215      throw new IllegalArgumentException(
216          "A mechanism's default command must require that mechanism");
217    }
218
219    if (defaultCommand.requirements().size() > 1) {
220      throw new IllegalArgumentException(
221          "A mechanism's default command cannot require other mechanisms");
222    }
223
224    var currentCommand = currentCommand();
225    BindingScope scope = BindingScope.createNarrowestScope(this);
226
227    var binding =
228        new Binding(
229            scope, BindingType.CONTINUOUSLY_SCHEDULE_WHILE_HIGH, defaultCommand, new Throwable());
230
231    var currentDefaultCommand = getDefaultCommandFor(mechanism);
232    m_defaultCommandBindings.computeIfAbsent(mechanism, k -> new ArrayList<>()).add(binding);
233
234    if (currentCommand != null && currentCommand != currentDefaultCommand) {
235      // User called `setDefaultCommand` inside another command.
236      // Immediately reprocess the default commands for this mechanism to ensure it's in sync with
237      // the rest of the commands in the scheduler. This is required because we normally schedule
238      // the default commands at the start of the scheduler `run()` method, so the new default
239      // command wouldn't be handled until the next run (ie, the previous default command would
240      // still be active for the current iteration)
241      //
242      // Note that we cannot do this if the current default command is the caller because commands
243      // cannot be canceled while mounted.
244      processDefaultCommands(mechanism);
245    }
246  }
247
248  /**
249   * Gets the default command currently used for a mechanism.
250   *
251   * @param mechanism The mechanism
252   * @return The default command, or null if no default command was ever set
253   */
254  public Command getDefaultCommandFor(Mechanism mechanism) {
255    var bindings = m_defaultCommandBindings.getOrDefault(mechanism, Collections.emptyList());
256    if (bindings.isEmpty()) {
257      return null;
258    }
259
260    return bindings.getLast().command();
261  }
262
263  // package-private helper for unit test access
264  List<Binding> getDefaultCommandBindingsFor(Mechanism mechanism) {
265    return m_defaultCommandBindings.getOrDefault(mechanism, Collections.emptyList());
266  }

268  /**
269   * Adds a callback to run as part of the scheduler. The callback should not manipulate or control
270   * any mechanisms, but can be used to log information, update data (such as simulations or LED
271   * data buffers), or perform some other helpful task. The callback is responsible for managing its
272   * own control flow and end conditions. If you want to run a single task periodically for the
273   * entire lifespan of the scheduler, use {@link #addPeriodic(Runnable)}.
274   *
275   * <p><strong>Note:</strong> Like commands, any loops in the callback must appropriately yield
276   * control back to the scheduler with {@link Coroutine#yield} or risk stalling your program in an
277   * unrecoverable infinite loop!
278   *
279   * <p>The coroutines provided to sideloaded functions will not cancel themselves if a fork or
280   * await call fails. This allows user code the opportunity to recover from a failure. You can opt
281   * into canceling the coroutine if a fork or await call fails by calling {@link
282   * Coroutine#setCancelOnForkFailure(boolean)}.
283   *
284   * @param callback the callback to sideload
285   * @see #addPeriodic(Runnable)
286   */
287  public void sideload(Consumer<Coroutine> callback) {
288    var coroutine = new Coroutine(this, m_scope, callback);
289    // Sideloaded functions shouldn't be canceled if a command can't be forked. The default behavior
290    // should allow user code the opportunity to recover from a failure. This differs from
291    // coroutines issued to commands, which should fail by default to prevent unexpected robot state
292    coroutine.setCancelOnForkFailure(false);
293
294    var scope = BindingScope.createNarrowestScope(this);
295    m_periodicCallbacks.add(new PeriodicCallback(scope, coroutine));
296  }
297
298  /**
299   * Adds a periodic callback to run as part of the scheduler. The callback should not manipulate or
300   * control any mechanisms, but can be used to log information, update data (such as simulations or
301   * LED data buffers), or perform some other helpful task.
302   *
303   * <p>For example:
304   *
305   * <pre>{@code
306   * scheduler.addPeriodic(() -> leds.setData(ledDataBuffer));
307   * scheduler.addPeriodic(() -> {
308   *   SmartDashboard.putNumber("X", getX());
309   *   SmartDashboard.putNumber("Y", getY());
310   * });
311   * }</pre>
312   *
313   * <p>{@code addPeriodic} is a convenience method that is identical to using {@link
314   * #sideload(Consumer)} with an unending {@code while} loop:
315   *
316   * <pre>{@code
317   * // An addPeriodic call:
318   * scheduler.addPeriodic(() -> leds.setData(ledDataBuffer));
319   *
320   * // Is equivalent to this sideload call:
321   * scheduler.sideload(coroutine -> {
322   *   while (true) {
323   *     leds.setData(ledDataBuffer)
324   *     coroutine.yield();
325   *   }
326   * });
327   * }</pre>
328   *
329   * @param callback the periodic function to run
330   * @see #sideload(Consumer)
331   */
332  public void addPeriodic(Runnable callback) {
333    sideload(
334        coroutine -> {
335          while (true) {
336            callback.run();
337            coroutine.yield();
338          }
339        });
340  }
341
342  /**
343   * Represents possible results of a command scheduling attempt. These can be used either as
344   * concrete results after a command was attempted to be scheduled, or as predictive results when
345   * checking if a command can be scheduled before committing to it.
346   */
347  public sealed interface ScheduleResult {
348    /**
349     * The command that was attempted to be scheduled.
350     *
351     * @return the command that was attempted to be scheduled
352     */
353    Command command();
354
355    /**
356     * Whether the scheduling attempt was successful.
357     *
358     * @return true if the scheduling attempt was successful, false if it failed
359     */
360    boolean successful();
361
362    /** Common interface for successful scheduling attempts. */
363    sealed interface Successful extends ScheduleResult {
364      @Override
365      default boolean successful() {
366        return true;
367      }
368
369      /**
370       * Gets the run ID assigned to the scheduled command when it was scheduled. If a successful
371       * scheduling result is created when checking if a command can be scheduled - but without
372       * actually scheduling that command - this will always return {@code 0}. Otherwise, a nonzero
373       * run ID will always be returned for a successfully scheduled command, even a one-shot
374       * command, guaranteeing that user code can always observe a run ID even if {@link
375       * Scheduler#runId(Command)} returns {@code 0} for that command.
376       *
377       * @return the run ID assigned to the scheduled command
378       */
379      int runId();
380    }
381
382    /** Common interface for failed scheduling attempts. */
383    sealed interface Failure extends ScheduleResult {
384      @Override
385      default boolean successful() {
386        return false;
387      }
388    }
389
390    /**
391     * A successful scheduling attempt.
392     *
393     * @param command the command that was successfully scheduled
394     * @param runId the run ID assigned to the scheduled command
395     */
396    record Success(Command command, int runId) implements Successful {}
397
398    /**
399     * A scheduling attempt that was redundant because the command was already running.
400     *
401     * @param command the command that was attempted to be scheduled
402     * @param runId the run ID assigned to the command when it was originally scheduled
403     */
404    record AlreadyRunning(Command command, int runId) implements Successful {
405      /**
406       * Gets the run ID assigned to the command when it was originally scheduled.
407       *
408       * @return the run ID assigned to the scheduled command
409       */
410      @Override
411      public int runId() {
412        return runId;
413      }
414    }
415
416    /**
417     * A scheduling attempt that failed because the command was lower priority than a running
418     * command with shared requirements.
419     *
420     * @param command the command that failed to be scheduled
421     * @param alreadyRunning the running command that prevented the command from being scheduled
422     */
423    record LowerPriorityThanRunningCommand(Command command, Command alreadyRunning)
424        implements Failure {}
425
426    /**
427     * A scheduling attempt that failed because the command was lower priority than a queued command
428     * with shared requirements.
429     *
430     * @param command the command that failed to be scheduled
431     * @param queuedCommand the queued command that prevented the command from being scheduled
432     */
433    record LowerPriorityThanQueuedCommand(Command command, Command queuedCommand)
434        implements Failure {}
435
436    /**
437     * A scheduling attempt that failed because the robot is in a disabled state and it requires one
438     * or more mechanisms that are not {@link Mechanism#controllableDuringDisabled() controllable
439     * during disabled}.
440     *
441     * @param command the command that failed to be scheduled
442     * @param unsafeMechanisms the uncontrollable mechanisms
443     */
444    record RequiresUnsafeMechanisms(Command command, Collection<Mechanism> unsafeMechanisms)
445        implements Failure {}
446  }
447
448  /**
449   * Checks if a command is able to be scheduled. Returns of the following states:
450   *
451   * <ul>
452   *   <li>{@link AlreadyRunning} if the command is already scheduled or running.
453   *   <li>{@link Success} if the command is not already scheduled or running and does not conflict
454   *       with any other scheduled or running commands. The associated {@link
455   *       ScheduleResult.Successful#runId() run ID} will be 0, rather than an actual run ID,
456   *       because the command will not have actually been scheduled and received an ID.
457   *   <li>{@link LowerPriorityThanRunningCommand} if the command has a lower priority than a
458   *       running command that shares requirements
459   *   <li>{@link LowerPriorityThanQueuedCommand} if the command has a lower priority than a queued
460   *       command that shares requirements
461   *   <li>{@link RequiresUnsafeMechanisms} if the command requires mechanisms that are not
462   *       controllable when the robot is disabled.
463   * </ul>
464   *
465   * @param command The command to check. Cannot be null.
466   * @return A schedule result indicating the schedulability of the command.
467   */
468  @NoDiscard
469  public ScheduleResult isSchedulable(Command command) {
470    ErrorMessages.requireNonNullParam(command, "command", "isSchedulable");
471
472    int id = runId(command);
473    if (id != 0) {
474      return new AlreadyRunning(command, id);
475    }
476
477    if (!RobotStateFetcher.getFetcher().isEnabled()) {
478      var uncontrollables =
479          command.requirements().stream()
480              .filter(mechanism -> !mechanism.controllableDuringDisabled())
481              .collect(Collectors.toSet());
482
483      if (!uncontrollables.isEmpty()) {
484        return new RequiresUnsafeMechanisms(command, uncontrollables);
485      }
486    }
487
488    Set<Command> ancestry = new HashSet<>();
489    for (var state = currentState(); state != null; state = m_runningCommands.get(state.parent())) {
490      ancestry.add(state.command());
491    }
492
493    return isSchedulableFromPriority(command, ancestry);
494  }
495
496  // similar to isSchedulable(Command), but used internally for processing bindings
497  // that may have command scopes.
498  private ScheduleResult isSchedulable(Binding binding) {
499    var command = binding.command();
500
501    int id = runId(command);
502    if (id != 0) {
503      return new AlreadyRunning(command, id);
504    }
505
506    if (!RobotStateFetcher.getFetcher().isEnabled()) {
507      var uncontrollables =
508          command.requirements().stream()
509              .filter(mechanism -> !mechanism.controllableDuringDisabled())
510              .collect(Collectors.toSet());
511
512      if (!uncontrollables.isEmpty()) {
513        return new RequiresUnsafeMechanisms(command, uncontrollables);
514      }
515    }
516
517    Set<Command> ancestry = new HashSet<>();
518    if (binding.scope() instanceof BindingScope.ForCommand(Scheduler _, Command parent)) {
519      for (var state = m_runningCommands.get(parent);
520          state != null;
521          state = m_runningCommands.get(state.parent())) {
522        ancestry.add(state.command());
523      }
524    } else {
525      for (var state = currentState();
526          state != null;
527          state = m_runningCommands.get(state.parent())) {
528        ancestry.add(state.command());
529      }
530    }
531
532    return isSchedulableFromPriority(command, ancestry);
533  }
534
535  private Scheduler.ScheduleResult isSchedulableFromPriority(
536      Command command, Set<Command> ancestry) {
537    var running = m_runningCommands.values();
538    Command conflict = lowerPriorityThanConflictingCommands(command, ancestry, running);
539    if (conflict != null) {
540      return new LowerPriorityThanRunningCommand(command, conflict);
541    }
542
543    conflict = lowerPriorityThanConflictingCommands(command, ancestry, m_queuedToRun);
544    if (conflict != null) {
545      return new LowerPriorityThanQueuedCommand(command, conflict);
546    }
547
548    return new Success(command, 0);
549  }
550
551  /**
552   * Schedules a command to run. If one command schedules another (a "parent" and "child"), the
553   * child command will be canceled when the parent command completes. It is not possible to fork a
554   * child command and have it live longer than its parent.
555   *
556   * <p>Does nothing if the command is already scheduled or running, or requires at least one
557   * mechanism already used by a higher priority command.
558   *
559   * <p>For purposes of scheduling, a child command is considered to have a priority equal to the
560   * highest priority in its scheduling hierarchy. For example, if a parent command with priority 10
561   * schedules a child command with priority 5, the child command will be treated as having a
562   * priority of 10 and will interrupt any conflicting command with a priority of 10 or lower,
563   * rather than the usual 5.
564   *
565   * @param command the command to schedule
566   * @return the result of the scheduling attempt. See {@link ScheduleResult} for details.
567   * @throws IllegalArgumentException if scheduled by a command composition that has already
568   *     scheduled another command that shares at least one required mechanism
569   */
570  // Implementation detail: a child command will immediately start running when scheduled by a
571  // parent command, skipping the queue entirely. This avoids dead loop cycles where a parent
572  // schedules a child, appending it to the queue, then waits for the next cycle to pick it up and
573  // start it. With deeply nested commands, dead loops could quickly to add up and cause the
574  // innermost commands that actually _do_ something to start running hundreds of milliseconds after
575  // their root ancestor was scheduled.
576  public ScheduleResult schedule(Command command) {
577    // Get the narrowest binding scope.
578    // This prevents commands from outliving the opmodes that scheduled them, or from outliving
579    // their parents (eg if someone writes a command that manually calls schedule(Command) instead
580    // of using triggers to do so).
581    BindingScope scope = BindingScope.createNarrowestScope(this);
582
583    // Note: we use a throwable here instead of Thread.currentThread().getStackTrace() for easier
584    //       stack frame filtering and modification.
585    var binding = new Binding(scope, BindingType.IMMEDIATE, command, new Throwable());
586
587    return schedule(binding);
588  }
589
590  // Package-private for use by Trigger
591  ScheduleResult schedule(Binding binding) {
592    var command = binding.command();
593
594    var result = isSchedulable(binding);
595    if (!(result instanceof Success)) {
596      // We check specifically for Success, instead of `successful()`, because only a Success
597      // indicates that the command can actually go through the scheduling process. AlreadyRunning
598      // means what it says on the tin, and it would be incorrect to run the command back through
599      // the scheduling process.
600      return result;
601    }
602
603    if (!(binding.scope() instanceof BindingScope.ForCommand)) {
604      // Track this binding so we can disable it when it's out of scope.
605      // Note that, even though triggers can clean themselves up, commands that are manually
606      // scheduled cannot do the same, so we have to track them in the scheduler.
607
608      // We don't bother tracking command-scoped bindings; the bound command will already be
609      // cleaned up in the same cycle that the parent command exits, so this would attempt to
610      // double-cancel a child command across two cycles (once when the parent exits, and then in
611      // the next cycle in cancelStaleBindings). That would cause problems if the command object
612      // is immediately rescheduled as cancelStaleBindings would immediately cancel the new run
613      m_activeBindings.add(binding);
614    }
615
616    // Evict conflicting on-deck commands
617    // We check above if the input command is lower priority than any of these,
618    // so at this point we're guaranteed to be >= priority than anything already on deck
619    evictConflictingOnDeckCommands(command);
620
621    // If the binding is scoped to a particular command, that command is the parent. If we're in the
622    // middle of a run cycle and running commands, the parent is whatever command is currently
623    // running. Otherwise, there is no parent command.
624    var parentCommand =
625        binding.scope() instanceof BindingScope.ForCommand scope
626            ? scope.command()
627            : currentCommand();
628    var state = new CommandState(command, parentCommand, buildCoroutine(command), binding);
629
630    emitScheduledEvent(command);
631
632    if (currentState() != null) {
633      // Scheduling a child command while running. Start it immediately instead of waiting a full
634      // cycle. This prevents issues with deeply nested command groups taking many scheduler cycles
635      // to start running the commands that actually _do_ things
636      evictConflictingRunningCommands(state);
637      m_runningCommands.put(command, state);
638      runCommand(state);
639    } else {
640      // Scheduling outside a command, add it to the pending set. If it's not overridden by another
641      // conflicting command being scheduled in the same scheduler loop, it'll be promoted and
642      // start to run when #runCommands() is called
643      m_queuedToRun.add(state);
644    }
645
646    return new Success(command, state.id());
647  }
648
649  /**
650   * Checks if a command conflicts with and is a lower priority than any running command. Used when
651   * determining if the command can be scheduled.
652   *
653   * @return The conflicting command, or null if there is no conflict
654   */
655  private Command lowerPriorityThanConflictingCommands(
656      Command command, Collection<Command> ancestry, Collection<CommandState> checkAgainst) {
657    int maxAncestorPriority = command.priority();
658    for (Command ancestor : ancestry) {
659      maxAncestorPriority = Math.max(maxAncestorPriority, ancestor.priority());
660    }
661
662    // Check for conflicts with the commands that are already running
663    for (var state : checkAgainst) {
664      if (ancestry.contains(state.command())) {
665        // Can't conflict with an ancestor command
666        continue;
667      }
668
669      var c = state.command();
670      if (c.conflictsWith(command) && maxAncestorPriority < effectivePriority(state)) {
671        return c;
672      }
673    }
674
675    return null;
676  }
677
678  /**
679   * Calculates the effective priority of a command, taking into account the priorities of its
680   * ancestors.
681   *
682   * @param state The command state to check
683   * @return The effective priority of the command
684   */
685  private int effectivePriority(CommandState state) {
686    int max = state.command().priority();
687    for (var parent = state.parent(); parent != null; parent = state.parent()) {
688      state = m_runningCommands.get(parent);
689      max = Math.max(max, parent.priority());
690    }
691    return max;
692  }
693
694  private void evictConflictingOnDeckCommands(Command command) {
695    for (var iterator = m_queuedToRun.iterator(); iterator.hasNext(); ) {
696      var scheduledState = iterator.next();
697      var scheduledCommand = scheduledState.command();
698      if (scheduledCommand.conflictsWith(command)) {
699        // Remove the lower priority conflicting command from the on deck commands.
700        // We don't need to call removeOrphanedChildren here because it hasn't started yet,
701        // meaning it hasn't had a chance to schedule any children
702        iterator.remove();
703        emitInterruptedEvent(scheduledCommand, command);
704        emitCanceledEvent(scheduledCommand);
705      }
706    }
707  }
708
709  /**
710   * Cancels all running commands with which an incoming state conflicts. Ancestor commands of the
711   * incoming state will not be canceled.
712   */
713  @SuppressWarnings("PMD.CompareObjectsWithEquals")
714  private void evictConflictingRunningCommands(CommandState incomingState) {
715    // The set of root states with which the incoming state conflicts but does not inherit from
716    Set<CommandState> conflictingRootStates =
717        m_runningCommands.values().stream()
718            .filter(state -> incomingState.command().conflictsWith(state.command()))
719            .filter(state -> !isAncestorOf(state.command(), incomingState))
720            .map(
721                state -> {
722                  // Find the highest level ancestor of the conflicting command from which the
723                  // incoming state does _not_ inherit. If they're totally unrelated, this will
724                  // get the very root ancestor; otherwise, it'll return a direct sibling of the
725                  // incoming command
726                  CommandState root = state;
727                  while (root.parent() != null && root.parent() != incomingState.parent()) {
728                    root = m_runningCommands.get(root.parent());
729                  }
730                  return root;
731                })
732            .collect(Collectors.toSet());
733
734    // Cancel the root commands
735    for (var conflictingState : conflictingRootStates) {
736      emitInterruptedEvent(conflictingState.command(), incomingState.command());
737      cancel(conflictingState.command());
738    }
739  }
740
741  /**
742   * Checks if a particular command is an ancestor of another.
743   *
744   * @param ancestor the potential ancestor for which to search
745   * @param state the state to check
746   * @return true if {@code ancestor} is the direct parent or indirect ancestor, false if not
747   */
748  @SuppressWarnings({"PMD.CompareObjectsWithEquals", "PMD.SimplifyBooleanReturns"})
749  private boolean isAncestorOf(Command ancestor, CommandState state) {
750    if (state.parent() == null) {
751      // No parent, cannot inherit
752      return false;
753    }
754    if (!m_runningCommands.containsKey(ancestor)) {
755      // The given ancestor isn't running
756      return false;
757    }
758    if (state.parent() == ancestor) {
759      // Direct child
760      return true;
761    }
762    // Check if the command's parent inherits from the given ancestor
763    return m_runningCommands.values().stream()
764        .filter(s -> state.parent() == s.command())
765        .anyMatch(s -> isAncestorOf(ancestor, s));
766  }
767
768  /**
769   * Cancels a command and any other command scheduled by it. This occurs immediately and does not
770   * need to wait for a call to {@link #run()}. Any command that it scheduled will also be canceled
771   * to ensure commands within compositions do not continue to run.
772   *
773   * <p>This has no effect if the given command is not currently scheduled or running.
774   *
775   * @param command the command to cancel
776   */
777  @SuppressWarnings("PMD.CompareObjectsWithEquals")
778  public void cancel(Command command) {
779    var currentState = currentState();
780    if (currentState != null && command == currentState.command()) {
781      currentState.coroutine().requestCancellation(); // yields internally
782      return;
783    }
784
785    boolean running = isRunning(command);
786
787    // Evict the command. The next call to run() will schedule the default command for all its
788    // required mechanisms, unless another command requiring those mechanisms is scheduled between
789    // calling cancel() and calling run()
790    m_runningCommands.remove(command);
791    boolean queued = m_queuedToRun.removeIf(state -> state.command() == command);
792
793    if (running) {
794      // Only run the hooks if the command was running. If it was on deck or not
795      // even in the scheduler at the time, then there's nothing to do
796      // Always run onExit first, in case cancellation has special behavior that overrides
797      // standard exit logic.
798      command.onExit();
799      command.onCancel();
800    }
801
802    if (running || queued) {
803      // Emit a cancellation event only if the given command was in the scheduler
804      emitCanceledEvent(command);
805    }
806
807    // Clean up any orphaned child commands; their lifespan must not exceed the parent's
808    removeOrphanedChildren(command);
809  }
810
811  /**
812   * Updates the command scheduler. This will run operations in the following order:
813   *
814   * <ol>
815   *   <li>Cancel any commands bound to scopes that have gone inactive, such as having been
816   *       scheduled in an opmode that's no longer selected on the driverstation
817   *   <li>Cancel any triggers that were created in scopes that have gone inactive, such as being
818   *       constructed in an opmode that's no longer selected on the driverstation
819   *   <li>Run sideloaded functions from {@link #sideload(Consumer)} and {@link
820   *       #addPeriodic(Runnable)}
821   *   <li>Update trigger bindings to queue and cancel bound commands
822   *   <li>Queue default commands for mechanisms that do not have a queued or running command
823   *   <li>Promote queued commands to the running set
824   *   <li>For every command in the running set, mount and run that command until it calls {@link
825   *       Coroutine#yield()} or exits
826   * </ol>
827   *
828   * <p>This method is intended to be called in a periodic loop like {@link
829   * TimedRobot#robotPeriodic()}
830   */
831  public void run() {
832    final long startNanos = RobotController.getTime();
833
834    // Cancel any commands with stale binding scopes
835    cancelStaleBindings();
836
837    // Unbind any triggers with stale creation scopes.
838    // This allows triggers that can never be used again to be garbage collected to reduce
839    // memory usage and avoid potential OOMs from poorly written user code.
840    unbindStaleTriggers();
841
842    // If the robot is disabled, cancel any commands that require uncontrollable mechanisms
843    cancelCommandsThatCannotRunInDisabled();
844
845    // Sideloads may change some state that affects triggers. Run them first.
846    runPeriodicSideloads();
847
848    // Poll triggers next to schedule and cancel commands
849    m_eventLoop.poll();
850
851    // Schedule default commands for any mechanisms that don't have a running command and didn't
852    // have a new command scheduled by a sideload function or a trigger
853    scheduleDefaultCommands();
854
855    // Move all scheduled commands to the running set
856    promoteScheduledCommands();
857
858    // Run every command in order until they call Coroutine.yield() or exit
859    runCommands();
860
861    final long endNanos = RobotController.getTime();
862    m_lastRunTimeMs = Milliseconds.convertFrom(endNanos - startNanos, Nanoseconds);
863  }
864
865  private void cancelStaleBindings() {
866    for (var iterator = m_activeBindings.iterator(); iterator.hasNext(); ) {
867      var binding = iterator.next();
868      if (binding.scope().active()) {
869        continue;
870      }
871      cancel(binding.command());
872      iterator.remove();
873    }
874  }
875
876  private void unbindStaleTriggers() {
877    // Remove strong references to any triggers that have gone stale. This allows triggers to be
878    // garbage collected if they're not referenced outside the scope that created them. We don't
879    // clear any command bindings or unbind it from the event loop; otherwise, cached triggers
880    // would stop being updated until new command bindings are added.
881    for (var iterator = m_boundTriggers.iterator(); iterator.hasNext(); ) {
882      var trigger = iterator.next();
883      if (!trigger.isScopeActive()) {
884        iterator.remove();
885      }
886    }
887  }
888
889  private void cancelCommandsThatCannotRunInDisabled() {
890    if (RobotStateFetcher.getFetcher().isEnabled()) {
891      // Nothing to do if the robot is enabled
892      return;
893    }
894
895    List<Command> commandsToCancel = new ArrayList<>();
896
897    for (var runningState : m_runningCommands.values()) {
898      var command = runningState.command();
899      boolean canRun = true;
900      for (var mechanism : command.requirements()) {
901        if (!mechanism.controllableDuringDisabled()) {
902          canRun = false;
903          break;
904        }
905      }
906
907      if (canRun) {
908        continue;
909      }
910
911      commandsToCancel.add(getRoot(command));
912    }
913
914    for (var queuedState : m_queuedToRun) {
915      var command = queuedState.command();
916
917      boolean canRun = true;
918      for (var mechanism : command.requirements()) {
919        if (!mechanism.controllableDuringDisabled()) {
920          canRun = false;
921          break;
922        }
923      }
924
925      if (canRun) {
926        continue;
927      }
928
929      commandsToCancel.add(command);
930    }
931
932    for (var command : commandsToCancel) {
933      cancel(command);
934    }
935  }
936
937  /**
938   * Adds a bound trigger to this scheduler. The trigger will be unbound from the event loop when
939   * its creation scope becomes inactive and may be eligible for garbage collection.
940   */
941  // package-private for Trigger
942  void addBoundTrigger(Trigger trigger) {
943    m_boundTriggers.add(trigger);
944  }
945
946  /**
947   * Removes strong retention for a trigger, allowing it to potentially be garbage collected if no
948   * other references to it remain.
949   */
950  // package-private for Trigger
951  void removeBoundTrigger(Trigger trigger) {
952    m_boundTriggers.remove(trigger);
953  }
954
955  private void promoteScheduledCommands() {
956    // Clear any commands that conflict with the scheduled set
957    for (var queuedState : m_queuedToRun) {
958      evictConflictingRunningCommands(queuedState);
959    }
960
961    // Move any scheduled commands to the running set
962    for (var queuedState : m_queuedToRun) {
963      m_runningCommands.put(queuedState.command(), queuedState);
964    }
965
966    // Clear the set of on-deck commands,
967    // since we just put them all into the set of running commands
968    m_queuedToRun.clear();
969  }
970
971  private void runPeriodicSideloads() {
972    for (var iterator = m_periodicCallbacks.iterator(); iterator.hasNext(); ) {
973      PeriodicCallback callback = iterator.next();
974      if (!callback.scope().active()) {
975        // The callback's enclosing scope exited - remove without running it and move on
976        iterator.remove();
977        continue;
978      }
979
980      // Update periodic callbacks
981      Coroutine coroutine = callback.coroutine();
982      if (coroutine.inUnmountableState()) {
983        // Nothing to do
984        continue;
985      }
986
987      coroutine.mount();
988      try {
989        coroutine.runToYieldPoint();
990      } finally {
991        Continuation.mountContinuation(null);
992      }
993
994      if (coroutine.isDone()
995          || coroutine.isInterruptRequested()
996          || coroutine.isCancellationRequested()) {
997        // Callback finished or requested early termination - remove it from the list
998        iterator.remove();
999      }
1000    }
1001  }
1002
1003  private void runCommands() {
1004    // TODO: Track command roots and run the commands in each root in reverse order, but run the
1005    //       roots in insertion order
1006    // Tick every command that hasn't been completed yet
1007    // Run in reverse so parent commands can resume in the same loop cycle an awaited child command
1008    // completes. Otherwise, parents could only resume on the next loop cycle, introducing a delay
1009    // at every layer of nesting.
1010    for (var state : List.copyOf(m_runningCommands.values()).reversed()) {
1011      runCommand(state);
1012    }
1013  }
1014
1015  /**
1016   * Mounts and runs a command until it yields or exits.
1017   *
1018   * @param state The command state to run
1019   */
1020  @SuppressWarnings("PMD.AvoidCatchingGenericException")
1021  private void runCommand(CommandState state) {
1022    final var command = state.command();
1023    final var coroutine = state.coroutine();
1024
1025    if (coroutine.inUnmountableState()) {
1026      // Nothing to do
1027      return;
1028    }
1029
1030    if (!m_runningCommands.containsKey(command)) {
1031      // Probably canceled by an owning composition, do not run
1032      return;
1033    }
1034
1035    var previousState = currentState();
1036
1037    m_currentCommandAncestry.push(state);
1038    long startNanos = RobotController.getTime();
1039    emitMountedEvent(command);
1040    coroutine.mount();
1041    try {
1042      coroutine.runToYieldPoint();
1043    } catch (RuntimeException e) {
1044      // Command encountered an uncaught exception.
1045      handleCommandException(state, e);
1046    } finally {
1047      long endNanos = RobotController.getTime();
1048      double elapsedMs = Milliseconds.convertFrom(endNanos - startNanos, Nanoseconds);
1049      state.setLastRuntimeMs(elapsedMs);
1050
1051      if (state.equals(currentState())) {
1052        // Remove the command we just ran from the top of the stack
1053        m_currentCommandAncestry.pop();
1054      }
1055
1056      if (previousState != null) {
1057        // Remount the parent command, if there is one
1058        previousState.coroutine().mount();
1059      } else {
1060        Continuation.mountContinuation(null);
1061      }
1062    }
1063
1064    if (coroutine.isCancellationRequested()) {
1065      cancel(command);
1066    } else if (coroutine.isDone()) {
1067      handleCommandCompletion(command);
1068    } else if (coroutine.getForkResult() != null) {
1069      handleCoroutineIRQ(coroutine.getForkResult(), command);
1070    } else {
1071      // Yielded
1072      emitYieldedEvent(command);
1073    }
1074  }
1075
1076  private void handleCommandCompletion(Command command) {
1077    command.onExit();
1078    emitCompletedEvent(command);
1079    m_runningCommands.remove(command);
1080    removeOrphanedChildren(command);
1081  }
1082
1083  private void handleCoroutineIRQ(Coroutine.ForkResult failure, Command command) {
1084    Command root = getRoot(command); // capture the root command before modifying scheduler state
1085    m_currentCommandAncestry.clear();
1086    emitForkFailureEvent(command, failure.getFailedCommands());
1087    cancel(root);
1088    Continuation.mountContinuation(null);
1089  }
1090
1091  /**
1092   * Handles uncaught runtime exceptions from a mounted and running command. The command's ancestor
1093   * and child commands will all be canceled and the exception's backtrace will be modified to
1094   * include the stack frames of the schedule call site.
1095   *
1096   * @param state The state of the command that encountered the exception.
1097   * @param e The exception that was thrown.
1098   * @throws RuntimeException rethrows the exception, with a modified backtrace pointing to the
1099   *     schedule site
1100   */
1101  @SuppressWarnings("PMD.CompareObjectsWithEquals")
1102  private void handleCommandException(CommandState state, RuntimeException e) {
1103    var command = state.command();
1104
1105    // Fetch the root command
1106    // (needs to be done before removing the failed command from the running set)
1107    final Command root = getRoot(command);
1108
1109    // Remove it from the running set.
1110    m_runningCommands.remove(command);
1111
1112    // Intercept the exception, inject stack frames from the schedule site, and rethrow it
1113    var binding = state.binding();
1114    e.setStackTrace(
1115        CommandTraceHelper.modifyTrace(
1116            e.getStackTrace(), binding.stackTraceStore().getStackTrace()));
1117    emitCompletedWithErrorEvent(command, e);
1118
1119    // Clean up child commands after emitting the event so child Canceled events are emitted
1120    // after the parent's CompletedWithError
1121    removeOrphanedChildren(command);
1122
1123    // Bubble up to the root and cancel all commands between the root and this one
1124    // Note: Because we remove the command from the running set above, we still need to
1125    //       clean up all the failed command's children
1126    if (root != null && root != command) {
1127      cancel(root);
1128    }
1129
1130    // Then rethrow the exception
1131    throw e;
1132  }
1133
1134  /**
1135   * Gets the currently executing command state, or null if no command is currently executing.
1136   *
1137   * @return the currently executing command state
1138   */
1139  private CommandState currentState() {
1140    if (m_currentCommandAncestry.isEmpty()) {
1141      // Avoid EmptyStackException
1142      return null;
1143    }
1144
1145    return m_currentCommandAncestry.peek();
1146  }
1147
1148  /**
1149   * Gets the currently executing command, or null if no command is currently executing.
1150   *
1151   * @return the currently executing command
1152   */
1153  public Command currentCommand() {
1154    var state = currentState();
1155    if (state == null) {
1156      return null;
1157    }
1158
1159    return state.command();
1160  }
1161
1162  private void scheduleDefaultCommands() {
1163    m_defaultCommandBindings.keySet().forEach(this::processDefaultCommands);
1164  }
1165
1166  private void processDefaultCommands(Mechanism mechanism) {
1167    var bindings = m_defaultCommandBindings.get(mechanism);
1168
1169    // Remove default command bindings that are no longer active.
1170    // If a default command is running when its scope goes inactive, also be sure to cancel it.
1171    bindings.removeIf(
1172        b -> {
1173          if (!b.scope().active()) {
1174            cancel(b.command());
1175            return true;
1176          }
1177          return false;
1178        });
1179
1180    if (bindings.isEmpty()) {
1181      // Nothing to do. No active bindings remain.
1182      return;
1183    }
1184
1185    // Cancel any default command except the narrowest-scoped one (the last binding in the list)
1186    for (int i = 0; i < bindings.size() - 1; i++) {
1187      Command widerScopeDefaultCommand = bindings.get(i).command();
1188      cancel(widerScopeDefaultCommand);
1189    }
1190
1191    if (!RobotStateFetcher.getFetcher().isEnabled() && !mechanism.controllableDuringDisabled()) {
1192      // Default commands can never be scheduled if the robot is disabled and the mechanism is not
1193      // controllable during disabled, so there's no point in attempting to queue the default
1194      // command
1195      return;
1196    }
1197
1198    // Check if the mechanism is currently in use. We can queue the default command if it's not.
1199    for (Command runningCommand : m_runningCommands.keySet()) {
1200      if (runningCommand.requires(mechanism)) {
1201        return;
1202      }
1203    }
1204    for (CommandState queuedState : m_queuedToRun) {
1205      if (queuedState.command().requires(mechanism)) {
1206        return;
1207      }
1208    }
1209
1210    // Nothing currently running or queued that needs this mechanism. Queue the default command.
1211    var defaultCommand = bindings.getLast();
1212    schedule(defaultCommand);
1213  }
1214
1215  /**
1216   * Removes all commands descended from a parent command. This is used to ensure that any command
1217   * scheduled within a composition or group cannot live longer than any ancestor.
1218   *
1219   * @param parent the root command whose descendants to remove from the scheduler
1220   */
1221  @SuppressWarnings("PMD.CompareObjectsWithEquals")
1222  private void removeOrphanedChildren(Command parent) {
1223    m_runningCommands.entrySet().stream()
1224        .filter(e -> e.getValue().parent() == parent)
1225        .toList() // copy to an intermediate list to avoid concurrent modification
1226        .forEach(e -> cancel(e.getKey()));
1227  }
1228
1229  /**
1230   * Builds a coroutine object that the command will be bound to. The coroutine will be scoped to
1231   * this scheduler object and cannot be used by another scheduler instance.
1232   *
1233   * @param command the command for which to build a coroutine
1234   * @return the binding coroutine
1235   */
1236  private Coroutine buildCoroutine(Command command) {
1237    return new Coroutine(this, m_scope, command::run);
1238  }
1239
1240  /**
1241   * Checks if a command is currently running.
1242   *
1243   * @param command the command to check
1244   * @return true if the command is running, false if not
1245   */
1246  public boolean isRunning(Command command) {
1247    return m_runningCommands.containsKey(command);
1248  }
1249
1250  /**
1251   * Checks if a command is currently scheduled to run, but is not yet running.
1252   *
1253   * @param command the command to check
1254   * @return true if the command is scheduled to run, false if not
1255   */
1256  @SuppressWarnings("PMD.CompareObjectsWithEquals")
1257  public boolean isScheduled(Command command) {
1258    return m_queuedToRun.stream().anyMatch(state -> state.command() == command);
1259  }
1260
1261  /**
1262   * Checks if a command is currently scheduled to run, or is already running.
1263   *
1264   * @param command the command to check
1265   * @return true if the command is scheduled to run or is already running, false if not
1266   */
1267  public boolean isScheduledOrRunning(Command command) {
1268    return isScheduled(command) || isRunning(command);
1269  }
1270
1271  /**
1272   * Gets the set of all currently running commands. Commands are returned in the order in which
1273   * they were scheduled. The returned set is read-only.
1274   *
1275   * @return the currently running commands
1276   */
1277  public Collection<Command> getRunningCommands() {
1278    return List.copyOf(m_runningCommands.keySet());
1279  }
1280
1281  /**
1282   * Gets all the currently running commands that require a particular mechanism. Commands are
1283   * returned in the order in which they were scheduled. The returned list is read-only.
1284   *
1285   * @param mechanism the mechanism to get the commands for
1286   * @return the currently running commands that require the mechanism.
1287   */
1288  public List<Command> getRunningCommandsFor(Mechanism mechanism) {
1289    return m_runningCommands.keySet().stream()
1290        .filter(command -> command.requires(mechanism))
1291        .toList();
1292  }
1293
1294  /**
1295   * Cancels all currently running and scheduled commands. All default commands will be scheduled on
1296   * the next call to {@link #run()}, unless a higher priority command is scheduled or triggered
1297   * after {@code cancelAll()} is used.
1298   */
1299  public void cancelAll() {
1300    for (var onDeckIter = m_queuedToRun.iterator(); onDeckIter.hasNext(); ) {
1301      var state = onDeckIter.next();
1302      onDeckIter.remove();
1303      emitCanceledEvent(state.command());
1304    }
1305
1306    for (var liveIter = m_runningCommands.entrySet().iterator(); liveIter.hasNext(); ) {
1307      var entry = liveIter.next();
1308      liveIter.remove();
1309      Command canceledCommand = entry.getKey();
1310      // Always run onExit first, in case cancellation has special behavior that overrides
1311      // standard exit logic.
1312      canceledCommand.onExit();
1313      canceledCommand.onCancel();
1314      emitCanceledEvent(canceledCommand);
1315    }
1316  }
1317
1318  /**
1319   * An event loop used by the scheduler to poll triggers that schedule or cancel commands. This
1320   * event loop is always polled on every call to {@link #run()}. Custom event loops need to be
1321   * bound to this one for synchronicity with the scheduler; however, they can always be polled
1322   * manually before or after the call to {@link #run()}.
1323   *
1324   * @return the default event loop.
1325   */
1326  @NoDiscard
1327  public EventLoop getDefaultEventLoop() {
1328    return m_eventLoop;
1329  }
1330
1331  /**
1332   * For internal use.
1333   *
1334   * @return The commands that have been scheduled but not yet started.
1335   */
1336  @NoDiscard
1337  public Collection<Command> getQueuedCommands() {
1338    return m_queuedToRun.stream().map(CommandState::command).toList();
1339  }
1340
1341  private Command getRoot(Command command) {
1342    Command root = command;
1343    Command parent = getParentOf(command);
1344    while (parent != null) {
1345      root = parent;
1346      parent = getParentOf(parent);
1347    }
1348
1349    return root;
1350  }
1351
1352  /**
1353   * For internal use.
1354   *
1355   * @param command The command to check
1356   * @return The command that forked the provided command. Null if the command is not a child of
1357   *     another command.
1358   */
1359  public Command getParentOf(Command command) {
1360    var state = m_runningCommands.get(command);
1361    if (state == null) {
1362      return null;
1363    }
1364    return state.parent();
1365  }
1366
1367  /**
1368   * Gets how long a command took to run in the previous cycle. If the command is not currently
1369   * running, returns -1.
1370   *
1371   * @param command The command to check
1372   * @return How long, in milliseconds, the command last took to execute.
1373   */
1374  public double lastCommandRuntimeMs(Command command) {
1375    if (m_runningCommands.containsKey(command)) {
1376      return m_runningCommands.get(command).lastRuntimeMs();
1377    } else {
1378      return -1;
1379    }
1380  }
1381
1382  /**
1383   * Gets how long a command has taken to run, in aggregate, since it was most recently scheduled.
1384   * If the command is not currently running, returns -1.
1385   *
1386   * @param command The command to check
1387   * @return How long, in milliseconds, the command has taken to execute in total
1388   */
1389  public double totalRuntimeMs(Command command) {
1390    if (m_runningCommands.containsKey(command)) {
1391      return m_runningCommands.get(command).totalRuntimeMs();
1392    } else {
1393      // Not running; no data
1394      return -1;
1395    }
1396  }
1397
1398  /**
1399   * Gets the unique run id for a scheduled or running command. If the command is not currently
1400   * scheduled or running, this function returns {@code 0}.
1401   *
1402   * @param command The command to get the run ID for
1403   * @return The run of the command
1404   */
1405  @NoDiscard
1406  @SuppressWarnings("PMD.CompareObjectsWithEquals")
1407  public int runId(Command command) {
1408    if (m_runningCommands.containsKey(command)) {
1409      return m_runningCommands.get(command).id();
1410    }
1411
1412    // Check scheduled commands
1413    for (var scheduled : m_queuedToRun) {
1414      if (scheduled.command() == command) {
1415        return scheduled.id();
1416      }
1417    }
1418
1419    return 0;
1420  }
1421
1422  /**
1423   * Gets how long the scheduler took to process its most recent {@link #run()} invocation, in
1424   * milliseconds. Defaults to -1 if the scheduler has not yet run.
1425   *
1426   * @return How long, in milliseconds, the scheduler last took to execute.
1427   */
1428  @NoDiscard
1429  public double lastRuntimeMs() {
1430    return m_lastRunTimeMs;
1431  }

1433  // Event-base telemetry and helpers. The static factories are for convenience to automatically
1434  // set the timestamp instead of littering RobotController.getTime() everywhere.
1435
1436  private void emitScheduledEvent(Command command) {
1437    var event = new SchedulerEvent.Scheduled(command, RobotController.getTime());
1438    emitEvent(event);
1439  }

1476  /**
1477   * Adds a listener to handle events that are emitted by the scheduler. Events are emitted when
1478   * certain actions are taken by user code or by internal processing logic in the scheduler.
1479   * Listeners should take care to be quick, simple, and not schedule or cancel commands, as that
1480   * may cause inconsistent scheduler behavior or even cause a program crash.
1481   *
1482   * <p>Listeners are primarily expected to be for data logging and telemetry. In particular, a
1483   * one-shot command (one that never calls {@link Coroutine#yield()}) will never appear in the
1484   * standard protobuf telemetry because it is scheduled, runs, and finishes all in a single
1485   * scheduler cycle. However, {@link SchedulerEvent.Scheduled},{@link SchedulerEvent.Mounted}, and
1486   * {@link SchedulerEvent.Completed} events will be emitted corresponding to those actions, and
1487   * user code can listen for and log such events.
1488   *
1489   * @param listener The listener to add. Cannot be null.
1490   * @throws NullPointerException if given a null listener
1491   */
1492  public void addEventListener(Consumer<? super SchedulerEvent> listener) {
1493    ErrorMessages.requireNonNullParam(listener, "listener", "addEventListener");
1494
1495    m_eventListeners.add(listener);
1496  }
1497
1498  private void emitEvent(SchedulerEvent event) {
1499    // TODO: Prevent listeners from interacting with the scheduler.
1500    //       Scheduling or canceling commands while the scheduler is processing will probably cause
1501    //       bugs in user code or even a program crash.
1502    for (var listener : m_eventListeners) {
1503      listener.accept(event);
1504    }
1505  }
1506}
